subject: Private deployment — localized data residency & audit requests (escalation)
messages:
From: Alyssa Martin <alyssa.martin@acme-health.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme-health.ai>, Diego Alvarez <diego@acme-health.ai>
Date: 2026-07-08T16:12:00Z
Subject: Private deployment: data residency & audit scope for pilot

Jonas — thanks again for the demo. We are ready to move to a paid pilot but have three binding requirements from security and procurement before we can sign the SOW: 

1) Data residency: All inference requests, logs, and derived telemetry must remain within our Frankfurt (eu-central-1) VPC. No telemetry may be routed to or stored in US regions.

2) Audit rights: Acme requires the right to commission a third-party auditor (once per quarter during pilot, then annually) to review environment configuration and access logs. Auditor must be permitted to inspect production logs and evidence relevant to model access.

3) Deployment constraints: We need HSM integration for key material, and a customer-managed private deployment (VPC peering or on-prem appliance) with no remote debug agents that exfiltrate logs outside the VPC.

Procurement is asking for a 25% pilot discount to offset integration costs and wants a 12-month committed term following pilot. Can you confirm Redwood can meet these controls and what exceptions (if any) you require? I’ve attached the draft SOW.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Alyssa Martin
Head of AI Ops — Acme Health Systems
Attachments: ACME-Pilot-SOW.pdf

Date: 2026-07-08T18:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deployment: data residency & audit scope for pilot

Alyssa — really appreciate the clarity on requirements. Short answers up front: we can do a Frankfurt-only deployment and we support customer-managed HSMs in Private, but the audit and telemetry asks need a quick internal review (primarily since quarterly third-party audits with full production log access are outside our standard addenda).

I’m looping in Rishi (deal desk) and Laura (head of Private deployments) to scope the redlines and propose an approval path. To keep things moving, could you confirm which logs the auditor needs (access logs, model input/output, or full raw payloads)? Also, what’s the proposed pilot length? That will influence acceptable discount levels.

I’ve attached a diff of our standard private addendum where I highlighted likely problem areas. We’ll come back with a recommended counterproposal and a path to executive sign-off if needed.

— Jonas

Subject: Fwd: Private deployment: audit / residency requirements (Deal: DEAL-20260708-ACMHEAL-042)

Folks — forwarding Acme’s asks and Jonas’ note. Key commercial points for review: 

• Audit frequency: customer asked quarterly during pilot, annual thereafter.
• Audit scope: production logs + model I/O. That has potential IP/exposure implications.
• Discount request: 25% for pilot (they want budget for integration).
• Deployment: Private with HSM + no telemetry outside EU.

Proposed internal positions: 
- Limit third-party auditor access to 1x/year (during pilot we can allow 1x with Redwood present), and scope to read-only copies of production access logs and environment configuration — not raw model payloads.
- Require NDA + approved auditor list and mutual written scope.
- Approve up to 15% pilot discount with a 12-month commit; anything >20% requires VP/CRO sign-off.

Attaching a short deal summary with ARR impact and our suggested redlines for legal. Need legal input on feasibility and recommended escalation.

Rishi
Deal Desk — Redwood Inference
Attachments: deal-summary.xlsx
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-10T15:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment: audit / residency requirements (Deal: DEAL-20260708-ACMHEAL-042)

Team — legal has reviewed the requested language. Our immediate concerns: unlimited or frequent third-party audits of production data is a material risk to other customers and to model IP. We can accommodate audited reviews under strict controls: 

1) Auditor scope: must be narrowly scoped to infrastructure configuration, IAM logs, and system access events. Raw model inputs/outputs are considered sensitive; access requires a specific written justification and data minimization (redaction or sampled records).
2) Frequency: limit to 1x/year standard; allow 1x ad-hoc during pilot subject to Redwood presence and a mutually agreed scope.
3) Logistics: auditor must be pre-approved, sign Redwood’s auditor NDA, and be accompanied by Redwood personnel for live inspections.
4) Operational requirement: customer-managed HSM and VPC isolated deployment is acceptable. We need CISO sign-off on the final architecture diagram.

Commercial: legal recommends approving a pilot discount up to 18% contingent on a signed addendum that codifies the audit scoping and approval process. Anything above 18% or requests for raw payload access triggers escalation to the CRO/CEO.

Attaching a redlines summary and a proposed addendum template.

— Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redlines_summary.pdf
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T14:02:00Z
Subject: Executive approval: Acme pilot commercial & security exceptions (DEAL-20260708-ACMHEAL-042)

Team — I’ve reviewed the legal memo and the deal economics. Executive decision: approve the Acme pilot under the following conditions only — please capture these in the addendum and SOW before routing to the customer for signature.

1) Discount: approve an 18% pilot discount (one-time credit applied to pilot invoice). Any request >18% must come back to me for explicit approval.
2) Data residency & deployment: Redwood will provision a dedicated Private deployment in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). All telemetry and logs will be stored in Acme’s VPC. HSM integration is required; engineering to confirm KMS/HSM architecture.
3) Audit rights: allow 1 independent third-party audit during the pilot window, subject to: (a) auditor pre-approval by Redwood, (b) execution of Redwood’s auditor NDA, (c) scope limited to infrastructure config, IAM/access logs, and redacted production evidence. No blanket access to raw model payloads. Redwood personnel must be present during any live inspection.
4) Commercial commitment: pilot acceptance must be followed by a 12-month committed contract to qualify for the discount.

Implementation & next steps: Jonas — confirm the SOW addendum with the redlines Marissa attached and send to Alyssa with the DocuSign link. Laura (Private deployments lead) — set up a technical readout for Acme’s CISO and schedule a KMS integration planning call. Rishi — update HubSpot and mark this as Executive Approved (18% discount).

I’m copying the customer-facing thread below when you send the addendum.

— Lauren Bishop
VP, Global Sales — Redwood Inference
